items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I remember sitting at Donte’s jazz club with Chuck Berghofer, a great bass player, and asking, “Chuck, what do you think I should do?”

ctx.x: Yeah okay, so you know. So if you either weren’t having a full college load or could convince them that you were nuts, or gay or something that would — or had a serious physical disability, you were drafted. And of course you had the option of enlisting so that’s what I ended up doing. I enlisted in this band. They actually recruited me, to be honest with you. So I did my Basic Training and came back and at that point of course I had the freedom to decide what I wanted to do. I went to USC for — intending to be a

music major, but I was so discouraged by the fact that there was no outlet for me to — I asked the professor when I signed up, “What are the chances of me putting together some kind of an ensemble?” I was already doing that. Okay? I already had a little band that I was writing for, kind of a Gil Evansy sort of an instrumentation, eight or nine piece. I forget what it was, band. So I proposed this to this guy, can I continue that kind of activity at an unused room at the school. And the guy looked at me and I…
Were there some aha moments, we might call them epiphanies now, but you mentioned something, we spoke briefly on the phone and you talked about a circumstance with Gerry Mulligan and Bob Brookmeyer.
